root_idea.summary: The root denotes something generated or produced from something else, especially foam or froth arising on a liquid.
root_idea.development: From the production of foam, related usages extend to churned butter, white blossom, intense whiteness, gifts, and other things understood as produced or brought forth.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole Quran-attested form group is displayed under the normalized nominal citation form زَبَدٌ.

senses.definition: Foam or froth formed on water.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence denotes the foam produced or carried by water; related Classical applications to other substances are listed separately.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feed someone fresh butter, or give him butter to eat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Transitive use with the person fed as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give someone a gift or give him some property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended use that may refer to giving a small amount or portion of one's property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike someone a blow or cast a missile at him hastily or quickly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be a blow or a shot or thrown missile; the haste is part of the reported construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To agitate a milk-skin so that its butter comes out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of churning or agitating the skin until the butter is produced.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To add fresh butter to parched-barley meal; an alternative interpretation takes the construction as swallowing the meal like butter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The second interpretation is explicitly reported as a disputed reading of the construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have froth or foam appear at the corners of the mouth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person, the construction describes foam appearing at the mouth in anger.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To separate or loosen cotton and prepare it for spinning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The operation may be done by hand or with a bow and wooden mallet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To speak in the same manner as another person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A relational construction comparing the speech of two people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To froth or foam, or cast forth foam, of a beverage, the sea, a cooking pot, a camel's mouth, or milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a Form IV intransitive or causative-state use describing the appearance or emission of foam.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a lote tree, to blossom and put forth a white product like foam; of a tragacanth plant, to put forth its growth and blossom.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from the white, foam-like appearance of the produce.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become intensely white.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended descriptive use based on the whiteness associated with foam.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To swallow something as one swallows a piece of fresh butter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended Form V use describing quick or easy swallowing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take the clear, pure, or choice part of something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of selecting or taking what is considered the best portion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take an oath hastily.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression for being hasty in taking an oath.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A gift.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended nominal use, especially in expressions concerning the acceptance or refusal of a gift.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fresh butter produced by churning milk; also a piece or portion of such butter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited lexical distinction uses the term chiefly for butter from cow, buffalo, sheep, or goat milk and gives another term for the product of camel milk; it also includes butter before clarification over the fire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The froth of milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This reading is explicitly presented as possibly arising from a textual error, so it remains a qualified Classical attestation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Metonymically, the choice or best portions—the cream—of discourse, a story, or similar material.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative plural-based use referring to what is considered the finest part.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An issue or event, especially one regarded as relishable or pleasing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported extended use applied to an especially agreeable event.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In broader Classical applications, foam, froth, spume, or scum on the sea, in a cooking pot, at a camel's mouth, on cud or spittle, or on silver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These applications extend the foam sense beyond the Quranic occurrence concerning water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pertaining to fresh butter; buttery.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A relational adjective formed from زُبْدٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Civet, as a well-known perfume.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term denotes the perfumed substance associated with the civet animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The civet or wild cat from which the perfume is obtained.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The animal application is reported as a figurative or metonymic use alongside the primary perfume meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fresh butter that has spoiled during churning; according to another report, thin milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The thin-milk interpretation is an explicitly attributed alternative.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The watery part of milk, the portion in which there is no good.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term contrasts the thin, less valuable part of milk with its thicker or better portion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Figuratively, a mixture of good and bad, or of truth and falsehood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proverbial use based on the mixing of the thick and watery parts of milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A plant of the plains with broad leaves, edible and considered good or pleasant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a separate plant name, with descriptions of its leaves, branches, and growth habit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Possessing or being a possessor of fresh butter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participial description derived from the butter sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Frothing or foaming; especially said of a tumultuous, foaming sea.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial adjective describing something producing or bearing foam.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Intensely white.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended adjectival use based on the whiteness of foam.

cautions: The Quranic noun زَبَدٌ denotes foam in the water passage; butter, gifts, perfume, and the derived verbal forms are distinct Classical lexical uses rather than additional Quranic senses.

Several Classical attestations preserve explicitly qualified alternatives, including the milk-froth reading under زُبْدٌ, the thin-milk reading under زُبَادٌ, and the alternative interpretation of the sawīq construction.
